questions.explain: At ±90° pitch, roll and yaw merge; that's why firmware uses quaternions.

questions.q: How many numbers and constraints does an attitude quaternion have?
A complementary filter trusts the gyro:
options: At low frequencies, like the accelerometer
questions.explain: The gyro is fast but drifts; the accelerometer is slow, without drift.

questions.q: What does Ki do in the Mahony filter?
questions.explain: The integral term converges to the constant bias.

questions.q: Why does yaw drift without a compass?
options: The accelerometer doesn't work on Z
questions.explain: You need an external source: compass, GPS course, GSF or external navigation.

questions.q: How does an EKF differ from a complementary filter?
options: An EKF doesn't use the gyro at all
questions.explain: A complementary filter is an EKF with a fixed K.

questions.q: Where is the primary attitude calculation in ArduPilot?
options: In EKF3; DCM is the fallback
questions.explain: The primary estimate is EKF3, DCM remains as a fallback.

questions.q: Why are Euler angles bad for calculations at θ = ±90°?
options: Roll and yaw merge into one degree of freedom
questions.explain: Gimbal lock: at ±90° pitch one degree of freedom is lost.
